record.paper_title: Highlights and Open Questions from ZEUS
record.original_question: For associated D* + dijet photoproduction with a sizeable low-x_gamma^OBS contribution, the massive next-to-leading-order calculation is significantly too peaked near x_gamma^OBS = 1 and underestimates the low-x_gamma^OBS cross-section. Is dynamical generation of charm in photoproduction sufficient to explain these data, assuming jet-hadronisation effects of about 10% are relatively less important?

evidence.quote: Here the measurement of xOBSγ has a relatively large contribution at low-xγ whereas the "massive" NLO calculation is significantly more peaked towards one, underestimating the low-xγ part of the cross-section. The question here is whether the dynamical generation of charm in photoproduction is sufficient, assuming that jet hadronisation effects, estimated at ∼ 10% using Monte Carlo simulations, are relatively less important.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider photoproduction of a charm meson $D^*$ in association with two hadronic jets at an electron–proton collider, in the kinematic regime of low photon virtuality ($Q^2 \approx 0$). For each event define the observable photon momentum fraction
$$x_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}} \;=\; \frac{\sum_{\text{jets}} (E - p_z)}{\sum_{\text{hadrons}} (E - p_z)},$$
where the numerator runs over the two highest transverse-energy jets and the denominator over all final-state hadrons in the laboratory frame. Events with $x_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}}$ close to $1$ are dominated by "direct" photon interactions, while a low value of $x_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}}$ indicates a "resolved" photon contribution in which the photon's partonic structure participates in the hard scatter.

Suppose that, in the measured differential cross section $d\sigma/dx_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}}$ for $D^*$ + dijet photoproduction, a sizeable cross section is observed at low $x_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}}$, while the fixed-order next-to-leading-order QCD prediction in the "massive" scheme (in which charm is treated as a heavy quark generated perturbatively from gluon splitting in the photon and proton, with no intrinsic charm parton distribution in the photon) is significantly more peaked near $x_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}} = 1$ and lies below the data at low $x_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}}$. Assume that non-perturbative jet-hadronisation corrections affect the parton-level prediction by at most about $10\%$ and may be neglected as a sub-leading effect.

Question: Is the purely dynamical (perturbative) generation of charm in the photon — i.e., charm appearing only through perturbative $g\to c\bar c$ splittings within the massive NLO framework, with no intrinsic charm content of the photon — sufficient to account for the observed low-$x_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}}$ enhancement of the $D^*$ + dijet cross section?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent HERA measurements and NLO analyses confirmed that massive (fixed-flavour-number) NLO calculations underestimate the low-$x_\gamma^{\mathrm{OBS}}$ cross section in $D^*$ + dijet photoproduction, while massless/variable-flavour schemes including a charm component in the photon describe the data better. However, no definitive consensus has emerged that dynamical (perturbative) charm generation alone, without an intrinsic/resolved charm distribution in the photon, suffices; the issue is interpretation-dependent and remains not fully settled in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of inclusive D*+- and associated dijet cross sections in photoproduction at HERA
status_evidence.snippet: A massive charm NLO parton level calculation yields lower cross sections compared to measured results in a kinematic region where the resolved photon contribution is significant.
status_evidence.claim: Massive NLO underestimates resolved-photon (low x_gamma^OBS) region in D* + dijet photoproduction.

status_evidence.title: Dijet angular distributions in photoproduction of charm at HERA
status_evidence.snippet: Both significant resolved and direct photon components contribute, with the resolved contribution indicating a significant charm component in the photon.
status_evidence.claim: Data suggest a charm component in the photon beyond purely dynamical generation, but interpretation is scheme-dependent.
